metaDescription: Six budget kitchen scissors, from multi-packs to a Japanese-steel pair and a two-piece KitchenAid set, compared on steel, cleaning and tools.
introParagraphs: Step up from the lowest tier and kitchen scissors start to diverge in design rather than just pack size. At this cap you can find a pair marketed with 2.0mm SK5 steel, a two-piece KitchenAid set with a nutcracker and bottle opener, and the familiar multi-packs from SZHLUX and Astercook alongside an iBayam two-pack. The question becomes whether you want one better-defined tool or several basic ones.

We evaluated the six listings on blade thickness where it is published, how the shears come apart or store, edge style, and what extra tools are built in. The trade is clear. A multi-pack gives you redundancy and, with the Astercook, color-coded pairs. A single premium-leaning pair gives you a clearer steel claim. A multitool set gives you function, but its extras can add bulk to a drawer.

What spending beyond this cap adds is a dedicated take-apart poultry design or blades around 3.5mm for joints. At this tier you are still buying general kitchen shears, so the useful goal is matching the pair to the way you cook rather than chasing the maximum steel spec. Each pick below is judged on what it does inside that limit and who should choose it over its neighbors.

products.name: Huusk Japanese Steel Kitchen Scissors
products.description:
Huusk is marketed as Japanese steel kitchen shears with 2.0mm SK5 steel blades, which places it between the 1.5mm thin-blade norm and the 2.5mm SZHLUX in thickness. The listing says the shears detach into a compact 9 inch size that slips into a drawer or picnic bag, so they come apart rather than hinging on a fixed pivot.

The handles are described as ergonomic and usable by left or right handed cooks, and the listing leans on gift packaging as a selling point. Be realistic about the Japanese-steel language. It is a marketing claim, and what you can verify is the stated 2.0mm thickness and the SK5 label, not an independent hardness figure.

That detachable design is the reason to pick Huusk over the multi-packs. Taking blades apart helps you reach raw poultry residue that a fixed pivot would trap, though you should confirm the exact mechanism on the product page. The SZHLUX offers thicker blades at 2.5mm and two pairs, so Huusk makes sense only if take-apart cleaning and a single well-defined pair matter more to you than extra spares.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a detachable, single-pair design with a stated SK5 steel claim.
pros: Detaches into a compact 9 inch form
Left or right hand use is stated
cons: Japanese steel wording is marketing, not a tested spec

products.name: KitchenAid 2-Piece Multipurpose Shear Set
products.description:
This KitchenAid set pairs two shears with extras. The listing describes a nutcracker and a bottle opener built in, alongside a design meant for opening packages, preparing poultry and stripping herbs from stems.

That makes it the only pick here where the shears double as small tools. For a cook who keeps reaching for a nutcracker or opener while prepping, that is real convenience, and ergonomic handles round out the package. The blades are described as razor-sharp, but the listing does not publish blade thickness or steel grade.

Compare it with the single KitchenAid All Purpose pair. That one is built around micro serrated blades and a sheath, while this set emphasizes versatility. A multitool shear usually trades a bit of cutting leverage for those add-ons, so it is better as an everyday kitchen helper than a poultry workhorse. Against the Astercook pack, you get two pieces and a brand name but not a color-coding system.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want the shears to double as a nutcracker and bottle opener.
pros: Nutcracker and bottle opener built in
Described for packages, poultry and herbs
cons: Multitool extras can reduce cutting leverage

products.name: KitchenAid All Purpose Kitchen Shears with Sheath
products.description:
The KitchenAid All Purpose pair is the simplest pick in this lineup. It features micro serrated stainless steel blades described as resistant to rust, a soft non-slip coated handle designed for extended use, and a protective sheath that covers the blades in a drawer.

The serrated edge is the practical advantage. Fine teeth keep the blades from skating over chicken skin, wet herbs and slippery packaging, which reduces the need to squeeze harder. Dishwasher safety adds to the convenience, although a dishwasher can dull budget steel over time, so hand washing remains the gentler option.

At this cap, the question is whether one pair is enough. The multi-packs give two or three, and the KitchenAid 2-Piece Set adds a nutcracker. Choose this single pair when you want the serrated grip, the sheath and one clean kitchen tool, not an assortment. Because the listing publishes no blade thickness, do not rely on it for regular chicken joint work. If you cook for a crowd and break down several chickens at once, the SZHLUX or a dedicated poultry shear will serve you better than this pair.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a simple serrated pair with a sheath and dishwasher cleanup.

products.name: SZHLUX 2-Pack Heavy Duty Kitchen Scissors
products.description:
SZHLUX publishes a 2.5mm stainless steel blade and contrasts it with traditional 1.5mm blades. That makes it the thickest listed blade among the general kitchen shears here, which is the property that reduces flexing against chicken joints and cartilage.

The pack includes two pairs and a protective cover, and the maker allows hand washing or dishwasher cleaning. The listing mentions meat, fish, bones, poultry, pizza and nut cracking, though the bone claim is generous for a 2.5mm blade. Dedicated poultry shears are usually thicker.

Against the Huusk at 2.0mm, SZHLUX has the stronger thickness number and an extra pair, while Huusk offers a detachable design. Against the Astercook, you get a stated thickness instead of color-coding. If chicken is your main cutting task and you want a sturdy pair that still costs little, this is the better value at the cap.
products.bestFor: Cooks who cut chicken often and want the thickest published blade in a multi-pack.
cons: Bone claims exceed what this thickness suggests

products.name: Astercook 3-Pack Heavy Duty Kitchen Scissors
products.description:
Astercook provides three heavy duty pairs, each with a different handle color. The listing suggests assigning one to meat and seafood and separate pairs to other foods, so the colors do real hygiene work without adding cost. Over time, a labeled system also stops family members from grabbing the raw-meat pair for fruit.

No blade thickness or steel grade is published, which means the pair is judged by build feel and the claims of reliable cutting performance and lasting sharpness. Those are maker statements, not measurements. If thickness is your priority, the SZHLUX at 2.5mm or the Huusk at 2.0mm offer a number.

The three-pack shines in shared kitchens and as a gift. Compared with the KitchenAid single pair, you trade serrated edges and a famous name for two spares and a labeling system. Compared with the iBayam two-pack, you get one more pair but not a published sheath, so check the page if storage safety matters.
products.bestFor: Shared kitchens that want three labeled pairs for the cap.
pros: Intended for poultry, meat, herbs and vegetables
cons: Sheath not stated in the listing

products.name: iBayam 2-Pack Kitchen Scissors, 8.5 in
products.description:
The iBayam is an 8.5 inch heavy-duty two-pack with hardened stainless steel blades. The listing says it handles cardboard, twine, food, meat, vegetables and poultry, and it ships with blade covers for safe storage.

Handles are soft comfort-grip, and the listing mentions cushioning pads. The sheath and the second pair are the main practical advantages, since the covers protect the blades and a spare protects the food pair from packaging duty.

Against the SZHLUX, the iBayam does not publish a thickness, so it is the more general-purpose pair. Against the Astercook it has one fewer pair but lists covers. It is the most balanced choice if you want spares and storage safety without a gimmick. In a household that already owns the KitchenAid pair, the iBayam spares are the cheap way to keep the good pair out of the junk-drawer jobs.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a spare pair, blade covers and no gimmicks.
cons: Pivot is not described as take-apart

buyingCriteria.explanation: Thickness decides how much a blade flexes against cartilage, so it is the best number for comparing shears. At this cap the published figures are 2.0mm for the Huusk and 2.5mm for the SZHLUX, against a 1.5mm figure the SZHLUX listing calls traditional. Poultry-specific shears are often around 3.5mm. If you cut chicken weekly, favor the SZHLUX. If you mostly open packages and trim herbs, thickness matters less.

A pivot that separates lets you clean raw-meat residue that otherwise sits in the joint. The Huusk listing says its shears detach into a compact 9 inch form. The other five picks do not advertise a take-apart design. If you prepare poultry weekly and care about hygiene, detachability is the feature worth paying for at this cap.

Micro serrations grip slippery skin, wet herbs and plastic packaging. Only the two KitchenAid listings emphasize a serrated or sharp design, and the All Purpose pair is the one that names micro serrated edges. The others describe plain sharp stainless blades. Choose serration if slipping is your main complaint, and a plain edge if clean paper-style cuts matter more.

A nutcracker or bottle opener is only valuable if you use it. The KitchenAid 2-Piece Set is the only pick with both, and it also advertises herb stripping. The extra functions can reduce leverage and add bulk. If you already own a nutcracker and opener, skip the multitool and put the budget into a thicker blade.

The SZHLUX and iBayam are two-packs, the Astercook is a three-pack, the KitchenAid 2-Piece Set has two pieces, and the Huusk and KitchenAid All Purpose are single pairs. A spare keeps one pair dedicated to food, which preserves its edge. At this cap, buy more than one pair unless you want a specific feature such as detachability or serrations. The Astercook three-pack is the extreme case, since one pair can always be in the dishwasher while another is in use.

Sheaths and covers prevent drawer nicks and tip damage. The KitchenAid All Purpose has a sheath, the iBayam has blade covers, and the SZHLUX has a protective cover. The KitchenAid All Purpose is dishwasher safe and the SZHLUX allows hand wash or dishwasher. Always dry the pivot after washing, because moisture is what dulls and rusts budget steel quickly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Published blade specs
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared published thicknesses and steel labels. The Huusk gives 2.0mm SK5 steel and the SZHLUX gives 2.5mm. The iBayam, Astercook and both KitchenAid listings do not state a thickness, so they were scored on other attributes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning design
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each pair can be taken apart or only washed whole. The Huusk is the only listing that says it detaches. The KitchenAid All Purpose is dishwasher safe, and the SZHLUX allows dishwasher or hand wash.

howWeEvaluated.title: Edge and grip
howWeEvaluated.description: Micro serrations on the KitchenAid All Purpose, ergonomic handles on the 2-Piece Set and Huusk, and soft comfort-grip handles on the iBayam were compared for how well they reduce slipping and hand strain.

howWeEvaluated.title: Versatility versus focus
howWeEvaluated.description: The KitchenAid 2-Piece Set adds a nutcracker and bottle opener. Everything else is a cutting tool alone. We weighed whether the extras justify the added bulk and any loss of leverage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The SZHLUX leads on thickness, the Huusk on take-apart design, the Astercook on pair count, the iBayam on storage with a spare, and the KitchenAid pair on edge type. We did not claim hands-on durability, so every ranking rests on listing specs and buyer feedback in broad terms.

faq.q: Which pick is best for cutting chicken?
faq.a: The SZHLUX at 2.5mm is the thickest published blade among the general kitchen shears here, so it handles chicken pieces better than the thinner options. The Huusk at 2.0mm is a step behind but detaches for cleaning. For whole spatchcocking, step up to a dedicated poultry shear, since the thicker steel and spring action there reduce hand effort noticeably. Chicken thighs, wings and drumsticks are a reasonable target for the SZHLUX.

faq.q: Is the Huusk really Japanese steel?
faq.a: The listing describes SK5 steel and Japanese metallurgy, but that is marketing language. What you can verify is the stated 2.0mm thickness and the SK5 label. Check the product page for the maker details before buying if origin matters to you. Either way, the value case for the Huusk is the detachable design and the 2.0mm blade, not the geography of the steel.

faq.q: Is the KitchenAid 2-Piece Set worth it?
faq.a: It is worth it if you will use the nutcracker and bottle opener. As a pure cutting tool it adds no more than the single KitchenAid All Purpose pair, which has micro serrated edges. Treat the set as convenience, not a stronger blade. Cooks who crack walnuts or open bottles while baking will notice the extras, and everyone else probably will not.

faq.q: Should I buy a multi-pack or a single pair?
faq.a: Buy a multi-pack if you want spares, because a dedicated food pair stays sharper when cardboard goes to a second pair. Buy a single pair if you want a specific feature such as detachability or serrations. The Astercook three-pack is the extreme case, since three pairs mean one can always be in the dishwasher while another is in use. At this cap you can afford either, so match the choice to the annoyance you want to fix.

faq.q: What does the next price tier add?
faq.a: Beyond this cap you move toward spring-loaded poultry shears with blades near 3.5mm and verified take-apart pivots. Those suit someone who spatchcocks birds or breaks down whole chickens often. For everyday kitchen work, the six picks here already cover packaging, herbs, chicken pieces and light poultry, so the extra spend mostly buys specialization.

The KitchenAid All Purpose listing says dishwasher safe, and the SZHLUX allows hand wash or dishwasher. For the others, check the product page. Even when allowed, hand washing is gentler on budget stainless and prolongs sharpness. Dishwasher detergent and heat are the usual causes of cloudy blades and loosened pivots.

faq.q: How do I clean shears after raw chicken?
faq.a: Open the blades fully and scrub the pivot with hot soapy water, then dry well. If the pair detaches, as the Huusk listing says, take it apart for a thorough clean. Keep a labeled pair for raw meat when you can, such as one pair from the Astercook set, and never use that pair for cooked food or fresh herbs.
